newsitem.title: UK: First 30-year rand Eurobond receives warm welcome.
newsitem.headline: First 30-year rand Eurobond receives warm welcome.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) launched the longest dated rand Eurobond at 30 years on Monday which was warmly received by investors, lead manager Toronto Dominion said.
"We're basically sold out of paper," a Tordom syndicate official said. "We're adding rand to our list of currencies and we'll be doing a number of rand deals this year."
"There's unbelievable demand for the product and the paper is very fairly priced."
Tordom -- a relative newcomer to the Eurorand market -- underwrote a two-tranche zero-coupon transaction for a nominal total of 7.5 billion rand for the triple-A rated EBRD.
The rand sector has burgeoned in recent weeks following a period of stagnation in 1996 when the South African currency slid on hard currencies and investors suffered heavy losses.
But recent issues have seen an enthusiastic response as investors in Asia, Britain, Canada and Europe prepare to take on the currency risk again.

The latest innovation in the sector has been the introduction of long dated zero coupon bonds. The maturities keep extending from the first such deal for the World Bank's private sector financing arm International Finance Corp launched at 10-years which yielded just over 14.0 percent to Monday's 30-year trasaction.
Today's deal will raise around $60 million equivalent for the supranational.
At fixed-price reoffer the 20-year tranche yields 14.39 percent annually while the 30-year tranche yields 13.65 pct annually.
The 20-year tranche was already increased on the day by 500 million rand to 2.5 billion rand.
"The market in rand is currently very good," the Tordom syndicate official said.

"There's an element of risk but the deal is priced to factor in that risk and there's even the possibility of going longer, even though one has to be more creative in how to hedge the issue as there is no equivalent domestic gilt."
The longest maturity domestic gilt, the R157, matures on 15 September 2015 pays a coupon of 13.50 percent and yields 15.18 percent.
Today's deal follows hot on the heals of the World Bank's zero coupon bond launched last week which was twice increased to 3.5 billion rand via Hambros Bank.
The World Bank bond was priced at 7.45 percent over 20-years while today's 20-year tranche was priced at 7.10 percent. Traders said the World Bank deal was seen as aggressively priced in comparison.
A trader at a U.S. investment bank said: "The issuer (EBRD) is reaching its LIBOR targets and the investors see the high interest rates with a low initial cost, but its a pretty big bet."
The deals have boosted sentiment in domestic South African bond markets ahead of the 1997/98 budget address on Wednesday.

A zero-coupon bond pays no interest over the life of the issue but is issued at a deep discount to face value. The difference between the issue and redemption prices creates a hefty capital gain which boosts the yield to market levels.
WestMerchant Bank is also waiting for an opportunity to launch a zero-coupon rand Eurobond, an official said.
